licence.scope: Archive data policy; no statement names these curves. SVO cites the ESO Filter Database at La Silla (http://filters.ls.eso.org/efs/efs_fi.htm), whose host no longer resolves (2026-10-26). Change to attribution if the archive policy is judged to apply by analogy. The curves are SVO Filter Profile Service records recovered from Internet Archive captures (svo2.cab.inta-csic.es did not answer on 2026-10-26); SVO states no licence (page footer '© SVO') and asks for the acknowledgement listed in info.json.

notes: Original-source curves (2026-10-26): XFilter DESCRIPTION: 'This Context allows to display the transmission of all ESO filters and the quantum efficiency of the ESO CCD ... Alain Gilliotte maintains up to date the filters database'. The .mt files are numbered sequentially; the ESO number is the FITS keyword FILENAME. Curves keep the full measured range (leaks, 1e-4 floor); SVO's copies are trimmed to the main passband. Licence/acknowledgements left to the Mac agent (see REPORT.md for the terms found). 0245, 0271, 0342, 0344, 0385, 0386, 0387, 0392, 0844, 0848 (2026-11-12): each curve is ESO's own La Silla scan of the filter over 300-1200 nm as ESO publishes it in the ESO-MIDAS calibration data (calib/raw/datatrans/filters/eso*.mt, whose FILENAME card names the ESO number; WFI filters from https://www.ls.eso.org/sci/facilities/lasilla/instruments/wfi/inst/filters/), including the near-infrared red leaks ESO records for the filter (PLEAK_NM/PLEAK_T and RLEAK cards, red-leak flag in filter.db; WFI table 'Does filter have a redleak?'). SVO's record of the same ID is this scan cut to the main passband, so its pivot and width leave the leaks out. 0212, 0340, 0674 (2026-11-12): each curve is ESO's own La Silla scan of the filter over 300-1200 nm (ESO-MIDAS calib/raw/datatrans/filters/eso*.mt), passband and the red leaks ESO records for it. SVO's record of the same ID holds only the near-infrared leak lobe of this scan and none of the passband, so SVO's pivot and width describe the leak.
